critical_code_review_comments: playerWrap (L422-428) correctly uses aspectRatio + overflow: 'hidden'. On web this maps to a padding-hack aspect-ratio container in RNW; the inner <VideoView> uses StyleSheet.absoluteFillObject and contentFit='contain', so portrait clips will letterbox with black bars inside the 16:9 frame (matches YouTube web behavior). Fix is minimal and correct.

closeBtn (L430-441) has zIndex: 5 but the VideoView renders nativeControls; on some browsers the native <video> controls may sit above the close button. Not part of this iteration's scope but worth noting for a future pass.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 16 was a small, surgical CSS-only fix on /app/frontend/app/video/[id].tsx: the video player wrap now uses aspectRatio: 16/9 + overflow: 'hidden' instead of a computed height from useWindowDimensions. This locks the frame to 16:9 on web so portrait sources letterbox inside (contentFit='contain') instead of stretching the container and overlapping the description/comments/tags below. No backend contract change, no new packages, no new testIDs. If a future iteration needs live-browser verification of the visual outcome, load /video/{id} of a portrait-source clip in a mobile-width web preview and confirm: (a) the player frame stays at width*(9/16) tall regardless of source aspect ratio; (b) title/actions/channel/description all sit strictly BELOW the player with no overlap; (c) close button (chevron-down) top-left remains tappable. All existing video testIDs (watch-close, watch-like, watch-share, watch-delete, watch-channel, watch-subscribe, watch-desc, watch-comment-input, watch-comment-post, watch-related-{id}) are preserved.
rca_of_issue: User reported description/comments overlapping the video on the web preview when the source was a portrait clip. Root cause was that {height: SCREEN_W * 9/16} on playerWrap didn't clip the native HTML <video> element inside, so it reserved its natural (portrait) aspect ratio and silently stretched its parent — pushing ScrollView content downward while still visually covering the video frame. Fix: switched playerWrap to aspectRatio: 16/9 + overflow: 'hidden' (locks the box) and let contentFit='contain' letterbox the portrait source. Removed the useWindowDimensions/SCREEN_W/playerHeight dead code. Verified via file grep (all 4 contract points satisfied), Metro 200, and 68/68 iteration-specific backend tests still green.
